references.text: Abraham received the command to circumcise all who were bought with money in his house, which establishes the basis for circumcised slaves participating in the Passover meal.
Confirms that a foreigner must be circumcised to eat the Passover lamb, the same principle applying to purchased slaves.
A priest's slave who was bought with money may eat of the holy offerings, having similar rights to participate in sacred meals.
The context forbids the uncircumcised from eating the Passover lamb, though verse 44 provides an exception through circumcision.
In contrast to the purchased slave: a resident alien and hired worker may not eat of the Passover lamb, since they are not part of the household in the same way.
Abraham circumcises all the men in his house, including those bought with money, as fulfillment of the covenant.
Genesis 17:13 gives the theological basis (the covenant) for the requirement of circumcision among purchased slaves in Exodus.
